Quick answer: the best eco-friendly Diwali corporate gifts in India are useful, reusable pieces made from natural materials — handwoven hamper baskets, bamboo trays, desk organisers and keepsake boxes — that replace plastic packaging and stay on the recipient's desk or table long after the festival.

Why companies are switching to sustainable Diwali gifts

  • Less waste: a handwoven basket replaces plastic or foil hamper packaging and gets reused.
  • Brand story: artisan-made gifts support rural livelihoods and fit ESG and CSR goals.
  • Memorable: each piece is handmade, so no two gifts are identical.

Diwali corporate gift ideas by budget

Under ₹500 per gift

  • Mini jute festive basket — fill with diyas or sweets
  • Kauna grass gift hamper basket (from ₹340)
  • Grass pen holder or mini desk vase (₹199)

₹500 – ₹1,500 per gift

  • Handwoven bamboo gift basket or square bamboo tray set
  • Sabai grass jewellery basket or round gift box
  • Water hyacinth desk organiser or catch-all tray

Premium (₹1,500+)

  • Oval Kauna grass jewellery box
  • Bamboo puja tray or serving tray
  • Partitioned cane organiser or keepsake box

Browse the full range: Corporate Gifts and Diwali Gift Hampers.

How to plan a bulk order

  1. Fix your budget per gift and the number of recipients.
  2. Order early — handmade pieces need lead time; aim for at least 3–4 weeks before Diwali for large quantities.
  3. Decide on fillers — sweets, dry fruits or diyas — and whether you want a thank-you note.
  4. Share delivery addresses (single office or individual homes).

Frequently asked questions

What is a good budget for employee Diwali gifts? Most companies spend between ₹300 and ₹1,500 per employee; client gifts are usually higher.

Are handwoven gifts durable? Yes. Natural fibres like cane, bamboo, Sabai and Kauna grass are strong and last for years when kept dry.

Can you deliver across India? Yes, we ship across India, with free shipping on orders above ₹1,300.

How do I get a quote? Contact us with your quantity, budget per gift and delivery date.

Quick answer: choose cane for the strongest, most structured baskets and furniture; water hyacinth for chunky, textured storage bins; Sabai grass for colourful coiled boxes, trays and wall plates; and jute for soft, budget-friendly mats and bags.

Comparison at a glance

Material Feel & look Strength Best for
Cane Smooth, glossy, structured Very high Laundry baskets, planters, trays, ottomans
Water hyacinth Chunky, rustic, golden-brown High Storage bins, placemats, organisers
Sabai grass Fine coiled weave, takes colour well High Gift boxes, trays, wall plates, bags
Jute Soft, earthy, flexible Medium Floor mats, table mats, wall rugs, bags
Kauna grass Light with a natural sheen Medium-high Hamper baskets, jewellery trays, bags

Cane

One of the strongest natural weaving materials. Ideal when the basket must carry weight or hold its shape. Shop cane.

Water hyacinth

Made from an aquatic plant harvested from waterways, giving it a strong sustainability story and a thick, tactile weave. Shop water hyacinth.

Sabai grass

A tough, low-water grass from Odisha and Bengal, hand-coiled into neat boxes and trays. Shop Sabai grass or read what is Sabai grass.

Jute

India's 'golden fibre' — soft underfoot and affordable. Shop jute.

Frequently asked questions

Which natural basket lasts the longest? Cane, followed by water hyacinth and Sabai grass, when kept dry.

Can natural baskets get wet? Occasional splashes are fine; avoid soaking and let them air-dry in shade.

Which is best for a bathroom? Cane or water hyacinth, placed away from direct water.

Which is best for gifting? Sabai grass boxes and Kauna grass hamper baskets — see our gift hampers.

Short answer: a madur mat is a handwoven mat made from Madurkathi grass (Cyperus tegetiformis), a GI-tagged craft of Paschim Medinipur, West Bengal. At GrassCrafts, Madurkathi puja and asana mats start at ₹399, table mats and runner sets at ₹300, a 6×3 ft quilted yoga mat is ₹1,699 and 3-fold quilted bed mats are ₹2,250–₹2,450. Shipping is free across India on orders above ₹1,300.

1. Types of madur mats

Type Typical size Best for GrassCrafts price
Puja / asana mat (dual-sided grass and cotton) 23 × 18 in Daily puja, meditation, festive gifting ₹399
Table mats and runner sets Sets of 4 or 6 mats, 48 in or 58 in runners Dining tables, festive hosting, hotels and cafés ₹300 – ₹950
Quilted yoga and meditation mat 6 × 3 ft Yoga, floor seating ₹1,699
Quilted bed and nap mats (3-fold) 6 × 4.5 ft Cool sleeping surface in summer, guest bedding ₹2,250 – ₹2,450
Fridge top cover 51 × 24 in Kitchen from ₹750

2. Why people choose madur over plastic or synthetic mats

  • Cool to sit and sleep on – the grass stays cool in Indian summers, which is why madur is a household staple in Bengal.
  • Natural and biodegradable – no plastic, no foam.
  • Light and easy to roll – easy to carry to a puja room, terrace or yoga class.
  • Supports a GI-tagged craft – Madurkathi weaving is centred in Sabang, Paschim Medinipur, and is largely done by women weavers.

3. How to tell a genuine Madurkathi mat

  • Fine, even strips of grass with a slight natural sheen.
  • A faint, earthy grass smell when new.
  • Small variations in colour and weave – every piece is handmade.
  • The seller can tell you where it was woven (Medinipur, West Bengal).

4. Choosing the right size

  • Single person puja or meditation: 23 × 18 in asana mat.
  • Yoga or floor seating: 6 × 3 ft.
  • Sleeping or a guest bed on the floor: 6 × 4.5 ft 3-fold bed mat.
  • Dining: 4 or 6 table mats; add a runner for a 4–6 seater table.

5. Care

Wipe with a dry or slightly damp cloth. Keep away from long exposure to water and harsh sun; if it gets wet, air-dry in shade. Roll rather than fold for long storage.

6. Buying madur mats in bulk

Madur asana mats and table mat sets are popular return gifts for weddings, Griha Pravesh and corporate Diwali gifting, and as hotel and café table settings. For 25 pieces or more, see our wholesale and corporate gifting page.

FAQ

What is madur mat made of?

Madurkathi grass (Cyperus tegetiformis), grown and woven in Paschim Medinipur, West Bengal. Some mats, such as our asana and quilted mats, add a cotton side for comfort.

Is a madur mat good for sleeping?

Yes. It stays cool and is widely used as a summer sleeping mat in Bengal. A 3-fold quilted bed mat adds cotton padding.

Can a madur mat be washed?

Do not soak it. Wipe with a damp cloth and dry in shade. Quilted cotton sides can be spot-cleaned.

How much does a madur mat cost?

At GrassCrafts, from ₹399 for a 23 × 18 in asana mat to ₹2,450 for a 6 × 4.5 ft quilted bed mat. Free shipping in India above ₹1,300.

By Sristi Dey, founder, GrassCrafts

Short answer: for bulk hampers, choose the basket by what goes inside first, then by budget. At GrassCrafts, handwoven Kauna grass hamper baskets start at ₹340, Kash grass hamper baskets and trays at ₹650, and cane hamper baskets at ₹1,599. Every one is handmade, plastic-free and reused long after the sweets are gone, which is why gifting companies, wedding planners and HR teams now ask for baskets instead of cardboard boxes.

This guide is for anyone buying hamper baskets in quantity: corporate gifting teams before Diwali and New Year, hamper studios and food brands that fill baskets themselves, and families or planners ordering for a wedding. It covers sizes, materials, real prices from our catalogue, what to put inside, and how to place a bulk enquiry.

What is a bulk hamper basket, and who buys them?

A hamper basket is the container a gift is built in: you buy the basket empty and fill it with sweets, dry fruit, makhana, candles, diyas or skincare. "Bulk" simply means the same basket (or a matched set of sizes) for many recipients.

  • Corporate gifting: employee and client hampers for Diwali, New Year, onboarding kits and dealer meets.
  • Hamper studios and gifting firms: they curate the contents and need a reliable basket maker behind them.
  • Food and gourmet brands: a reusable basket makes a festive pack look premium without a printed box.
  • Weddings: return gifts for guests, Haldi and Mehendi baskets, and trousseau (tattva) packing.
  • Real-estate developers and hotels: housewarming or key-handover gifts, and welcome or amenity baskets.

Which material is right for a hamper basket?

Each natural fibre gives a different look and strength. Here is how the materials we weave compare for hamper use.

Material Look Best for GrassCrafts price (each)
Kauna grass (Manipur) Glossy, golden reed with a braided handle Return gifts, small corporate hampers, chocolates and jewellery ₹340 – ₹599
Kash grass (Bengal) Light beige, fine coil weave, net-top or tray styles Wedding hampers, dry-fruit trays, open presentation ₹650 – ₹765
Straw and grass Natural, rustic, often in festive colours Haldi, Mehendi and Godh Bharai hampers ₹550 – ₹1,050
Sabai grass Earthy, twisted-rope texture, lidded or framed styles Lidded hampers, fruit and kitchen gifts ₹699 – ₹1,450
Water hyacinth Chunky, soft, rectangular with handles Large family hampers, home-décor gifts ₹1,199 – ₹1,599
Cane Strong, structured, premium finish Trousseau baskets, VIP client hampers, heavy contents ₹1,599 (hamper baskets)

Prices are the current retail prices on grasscrafts.com for single pieces. For quantities, ask us for a quote (details below).

Which hamper basket should I choose for my budget?

Most buyers work backwards from a per-gift budget. The basket is usually a modest share of the total, so pick the basket that suits the contents and the recipient.

Basket Size / options Price Good for
Kauna grass round hamper basket 6 in diameter × 4 in high; with or without handle ₹340 – ₹599 Return gifts, small chocolate or makhana packs
Square Kauna grass hamper basket Square ₹380 – ₹399 Stationery or skincare sets
Handwoven wedding gift hamper basket (Kash) One size ₹650 Wedding and festive hampers
Kash grass net-top rectangular basket 12 × 6 × 4 in ₹765 Dry-fruit rows, sweets boxes, diyas
Sabai grass lidded basket with wooden handle Small / Medium / Large ₹699 – ₹940 Closed hampers that travel well
Straw wedding gift hamper basket One size ₹1,050 Family hampers, Godh Bharai
Water hyacinth storage basket Small / Medium / Big ₹1,199 – ₹1,599 Large hampers that become home storage
Cane wedding gift hamper basket One size ₹1,599 Trousseau packing, senior client gifts

How do I choose the right hamper basket size?

  1. Lay out the contents first. Put every item together on a table and measure the footprint and the tallest piece.
  2. Match the item count. As a rough guide, a small basket suits 2–3 items, a medium basket 3–5, and a large basket 5–7 or more.
  3. Leave room for filler. Allow a little extra width for shredded paper, a cloth liner or dried flowers, and make sure the tallest item sits a little below the rim (or below the lid on a lidded basket).
  4. Think about the journey. If hampers will be couriered across India, a lidded Sabai basket or a structured cane basket protects contents better than an open tray.
  5. Order one sample size set first. Handwoven pieces vary slightly in size and shade. That is part of their charm, but check the fit with your real contents before you finalise a large order.

What should I put inside a Diwali or corporate hamper?

  • Diwali: dry fruit in jute or cloth pouches, diyas, a candle, sweets, and a handwritten card.
  • Corporate (no food): some companies ask for eco gifts with no food. A good set is a handwoven basket with a desk organiser, a planter or a set of table mats.
  • New Year client gifts: tea or coffee, a notebook, and a small planter in a lidded basket.
  • Wedding return gifts: makhana or dry fruit, a sweet box and a thank-you card. See our wedding return gift basket guide for ceremony-by-ceremony ideas.
  • Housewarming / key handover: a basket with a planter, a puja mat or a set of coasters, so the gift becomes part of the new home.

Tip: line the basket with a cotton napkin or a Madurkathi table mat. Madurkathi is a GI-tagged Bengal craft (GI no. 567, listed on the IP India Geographical Indications registry), and the mat becomes part of the gift.

Why choose handwoven baskets over boxes for bulk gifting?

  • They are kept. A basket becomes a fruit basket, a puja tray or desk storage, so your brand or family name stays in view.
  • Plastic-free and biodegradable. Natural grass, reed and cane, with no foam or plastic film needed.
  • Made by Indian artisans. Kauna is woven in Manipur, Kash and straw in Bengal, and cane by traditional cane weavers. Supporting handicrafts is part of India's wider craft promotion work (see the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts)).
  • They photograph well. Natural textures look rich in unboxing photos and social posts, without the cost of metal or velvet boxes.

How do I care for handwoven hamper baskets?

  • Keep them dry. Wipe with a dry or slightly damp cloth, never soak them.
  • If a basket gets damp, air-dry it in shade, not harsh sun.
  • Store hampers in a cool, airy place before dispatch, not in sealed plastic for long periods.
  • Use a liner or pouch for oily sweets or loose powders so the weave stays clean.

How do I order hamper baskets in bulk from GrassCrafts?

  • Tell us the quantity, occasion, delivery city and date you need them by.
  • Say which basket (or which size mix) you like. Mixed orders are possible, for example cane for senior clients and Kauna for the wider team.
  • Order early: every piece is handmade, and the Diwali and wedding season is our busiest time. We confirm availability and timing with your quote.
  • Gifting firms, hamper studios and planners who order regularly can ask us about trade pricing.

Ordering in bulk for a wedding, hotel or company? WhatsApp +91 62907 44782 or use our wholesale and corporate gifting page. You can also browse our corporate gifts, Diwali gift hampers and wedding gift hampers.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I buy hamper baskets in bulk in India?

You can order handwoven hamper baskets in bulk directly from makers such as GrassCrafts. Share the quantity, occasion, city and date through our wholesale page or on WhatsApp (+91 62907 44782) for a quote.

How much does a handwoven hamper basket cost?

At GrassCrafts, single-piece retail prices start at ₹340 for a Kauna grass hamper basket, ₹650 for Kash grass hamper baskets and trays, and go up to ₹1,599 for a cane hamper basket.

Which basket is best for Diwali hampers?

For small hampers of sweets or dry fruit, a Kauna grass or Kash grass basket. For larger hampers that are couriered, a lidded Sabai grass basket or a cane basket protects the contents better.

What size hamper basket do I need?

Lay out the contents and measure them. A small basket suits 2–3 items, a medium 3–5 and a large 5–7 or more. Leave a little room for filler and keep the tallest item below the rim or lid.

Are grass hamper baskets reusable?

Yes. After the gift is opened, the basket works as a fruit basket, puja tray, planter cover or storage basket.

Can I mix basket sizes and materials in one bulk order?

Yes. Many buyers order one style for the wider team or guests and a premium cane basket for family or senior clients. Tell us the mix when you ask for a quote.

Can gifting companies and hamper studios buy empty baskets from GrassCrafts?

Yes. We supply empty handwoven baskets for others to fill. Contact us on WhatsApp or through the wholesale page and ask about trade pricing.

body:
The simplest way to decorate baskets for Haldi and Mehendi is to keep the weave visible and add colour with flowers, fabric and ribbon: yellow and marigold for Haldi, green and pink for Mehendi. A handwoven grass or cane basket then works as the decor, the packing and a reusable return gift in one.

By Sristi Dey, founder, GrassCrafts

Why use baskets for Haldi and Mehendi ceremonies?

Both functions run on small, repeated moments: handing out flowers, offering haldi, giving favours to guests. A basket holds all of that, photographs well, and guests can reuse it at home. A natural-fibre basket is also plastic-free and works against almost any outfit colour.

How do you decorate a basket for a Haldi ceremony?

Which colours and flowers suit Haldi?

Stay with yellow, orange and white. Marigold garlands tied around the rim, a few jasmine strands and a small bundle of fresh leaves are enough. Let the natural straw show through, because it matches the warm tones.

What can go inside a Haldi basket?

  • Fresh petals for the guests to throw or tuck into hair.
  • Small bowls or a cloth pouch for haldi paste.
  • A thin cotton cloth in yellow as a liner.

Which GrassCrafts baskets work for Haldi?

Our Haldi ceremony gift hampers include a round grass basket in small (from ₹550) and medium (from ₹1,050), and a cane Haldi hamper basket (from ₹1,599).

How do you decorate baskets for a Mehendi ceremony?

Which colours suit Mehendi?

Green, pink and orange. Wrap the handle with a green ribbon or dupatta strip, add a few bangles or small tassels, and tie a tag with the guest's name.

What can go inside a Mehendi basket?

  • Mehendi cones, set out for the guests.
  • Bangles, a hair accessory or a small sweet box as the favour.
  • Tissue or shredded paper in a matching shade so the weave stays the star.

Which GrassCrafts baskets work for Mehendi?

Browse the Mehendi ceremony gift hampers: straw baskets in small (from ₹550) and medium (from ₹699), and a cane Mehendi hamper basket (from ₹1,599).

Which basket should you pick: straw, grass or cane?

Basket Best for Price from
Round grass Haldi basket, small Individual guest favours ₹550
Straw Mehendi basket, small Individual guest favours ₹550
Straw Mehendi basket, medium A fuller favour with sweets and bangles ₹699
Round grass Haldi basket, medium Family and close-guest hampers ₹1,050
Cane Haldi or Mehendi hamper basket Bride and groom's families, display pieces ₹1,599

Prices are the starting prices on our website today and can change. For a full wedding set, see our wedding gift hampers or our guide to wedding return gift baskets.

How do you set up the baskets step by step?

  1. Count your guests first. Decide how many favour baskets you need, plus a few extra for family and helpers.
  2. Pick one colour story per ceremony. Yellow and white for Haldi, green and pink for Mehendi keeps the table tidy in photographs.
  3. Line each basket. Use cloth or tissue so the weave stays clean.
  4. Fill and tag. Add the favour, then a small tag with a name or a thank-you line.
  5. Dress the rim last. Tie flowers, ribbon or a small tassel just before the guests arrive so fresh flowers stay fresh.

What are good ideas by budget?

Small favour baskets

Choose the small grass or straw baskets (from ₹550 each on our website) and fill them with one sweet box, a hair accessory or a few bangles. A ribbon and a tag are enough decoration.

Hampers for close family

Choose a medium basket or a cane hamper basket and layer in dry fruits, a candle, a small decor piece and a handwritten note. Cane holds its shape well, so it also works as a display piece on a side table.

Decor-only baskets

Baskets do not have to be gifts. Use larger ones to hold petals at the entrance, to stack Mehendi cones, or to carry the haldi bowls to the stage.

What do guests do with the basket afterwards?

This is the main reason to prefer woven baskets over a one-use box. Guests can keep fruit, toiletries, keys, toys or yarn in them. It is a gift that stays in the house and is noticed again.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Overfilling a small basket until the weave strains.
  • Putting wet flowers or paste directly on the straw.
  • Leaving baskets in damp storage after the function.
  • Ordering at the last minute. Wedding season runs from mid-November to mid-December, so plan early.

How do you choose and care for the baskets?

  • Match the size to the contents. Small for a favour and a sweet, medium for several items, cane for gifts to family.
  • Keep them dry. Wipe with a dry or barely damp cloth and keep away from standing water.
  • Use a liner. A cloth or paper liner protects the weave from haldi stains and mehendi paste.
  • Store flat and dry after the function; they can be reused for storage, fruit or festival gifting.

Ordering in bulk for a wedding? WhatsApp +91 62907 44782.

Frequently asked questions

What should I put in a Haldi ceremony basket?

Fresh petals, a small bowl for haldi paste and a yellow cloth liner are the usual basics, with a favour for guests if the basket doubles as a return gift.

What colours are best for Mehendi decoration?

Green, pink and orange are the most common. Natural straw looks good with all three.

Can I use one basket for both ceremonies?

Yes. Change the ribbon and flowers: marigold and yellow for Haldi, green and pink for Mehendi.

Are the baskets reusable?

Yes. They are handwoven from natural grass, straw or cane and can be reused for storage or gifting once the function is over.

How do I keep haldi from staining the basket?

Line it with cloth or paper, and keep wet paste in a bowl inside rather than directly on the weave.

Do you take bulk orders for weddings?

Yes, message us on WhatsApp +91 62907 44782 with your function date and the number of guests.
